chunks: And it is narrated from Shihāb ibn ʿAbd Rabbih that he said:
I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “I take suḥūr with chicks that are brought from outside Makkah, then slaughtered in the Sanctuary, and I take suḥūr with them.”
So he عليه السلام said: “What an evil suḥūr your suḥūr is! Did you not know that whatever you brought into the Sanctuary alive has become forbidden for you to slaughter and to keep?”

key_terms.الْحَرَمِ: the Sacred Sanctuary of Makkah, where special legal restrictions apply
key_terms.بِفِرَاخٍ: with chicks or young birds used here as the animals in question

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to slaughter birds brought alive into the Haram of Makkah?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling concerning the Sacred Sanctuary: an animal brought into the Haram alive may not then be slaughtered or retained there. The Imam عليه السلام condemns the practice plainly, showing the sanctity of the Haram and the special restrictions that apply within it.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.2370 - Shihab ibn Abd Rabbihi narrated:
"I said to Abu Abdullah (as): 'I partake in Suhoor with chicks brought from outside Mecca, which are slaughtered in the Sacred Sanctuary, and I partake in Suhoor with them.'
Imam (as) replied: 'What an evil Suhoor is your Suhoor! Do you not know that whatever you bring into the Sacred Sanctuary alive becomes forbidden for you to slaughter and to retain?'"
